routes.name: South Sudan e-Visa
routes.summary: Apply online on the official e-visa portal, pay by card, and download the e-visa PDF. Show it at entry.

other: The portal did not list fees, eligibility rules or document requirements. Check the portal before applying.

steps: Create an account on the e-visa portal
Pay the application fee by card
Show it to the immigration officer on arrival
routes.processing: The portal says you can download the e-visa PDF within 72 hours.

routes.name: Single or Multiple Entry Visa (embassy)
routes.summary: For travelers from countries that need a visa. Apply at a South Sudan embassy or consulate. Some nationals are visa exempt under bilateral deals, and some can get a visa on arrival, but the ministry page does not list them.

other: Fees, validity and documents not stated on the official page.

sources.label: South Sudan Foreign Ministry: types of visas

routes.name: Transit Visa
routes.summary: For people passing through to another destination. Generally issued for no more than 72 hours.

routes.name: Residence Permits (Temporary, Ordinary, Special)
routes.summary: Three tiers under the Passports and Immigration Act 2011. Temporary permits run up to 12 months. Ordinary permits run 2 years. Special permits run 5 years.

other: Temporary: anyone who does not qualify for the other two.
Ordinary: 5 years of continuous residence, or over 2 years of lawful stay plus valuable scientific, technical or commercial activity.
Special: 3 years of continuous residence, or over 5 years of lawful stay plus valuable activity.
The permit covers the spouse, children and dependants.
Fees and work permit rules are not in the Act. Confirm with the Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration.

stay.note: Temporary up to 12 months, ordinary 2 years, special 5 years, all renewable. Ordinary and special permits lapse after 6 months abroad without a return visa.

routes.name: Refugee and Asylum Process
routes.summary: Political refugees and asylum seekers are covered by personal exemptions in the immigration law. A separate Refugee Act 2012 governs the process. Details were not confirmed.

other: Process details not read. Contact the Commission for Refugee Affairs or UNHCR.
